The ALTS Mode is always armed except when ALT, GS, or GA Mode is active. When the vertical Mode is GA, ALTS is armed if the preselected altitude is greater than the current altitude by 75 ft. Rotating the ALT knob inhibits ALTS to prevent altitude capture during preselected altitude change. The ALTS Mode is activated during altitude capture when a new altitude is selected or the current altitude is maintained. The Altitude Hold Mode (ALT) holds the aircraft at a selected altitude.

In the VS Mode, the Autoflight System generates commands to maintain the VS reference. The PITCH/VS Wheel is used to change the VS reference, with slow rotation changing the VS reference by 100 ft/min per click and quick rotation by more than 100 ft/min per click. The vertical speed reference is limited to ± 8000 ft/min. The AT controls airspeed in VS Mode.

The GA Mode can be deselected by changing the FG coupled side, manually selecting other lateral modes, or by engaging the AP or pressing the SYNC Pushbutton on either side. To select GA Mode, press the TOGA Pushbutton when the aircraft is in flight.
The OSPD Mode automatically activates when the aircraft Mach number is more than Mmo + 0.01, or the airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt, to generate pitch commands to reduce airspeed below Vmo/Mmo.

The Underspeed (USPD) Mode is automatically activated when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01, unless ALTS mode is captured or ALT mode is active. It provides pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman. It automatically deactivates when airspeed/Mach is greater than Vman/Mman, switching the vertical mode to FLC and setting the airspeed reference to Vman + 5 kt/Mman +0.01. The SPEED Knob is inhibited while USPD mode is active. It can be deselected manually by selecting another vertical mode when airspeed is above Vman - 5 kt or Mman - 0.01 M, or it exits automatically when airspeed increases to Vman/Mman.

Responses: VNAV CLIMB
VNAV provides references for vertical modes and allows the Autoflight System to follow FMS vertical profile constraints.

If the preselect altitude is not raised to the flight plan target altitude or above, it will be captured, causing the mode to sequence to VALTS. When preselect altitude is eventually raised, VNAV will not sequence to climb VFLC until a climb mode selection is made. If the aircraft is at a constraint altitude and the preselected altitude is raised, an altitude change mode (FLC, VS, or PTCH) is selected, VNAV allows the aircraft to leave the constraint altitude. However, if the constraint is AT, AT OR BELOW, or BETWEEN, CHECK FPLN ALT is displayed. If the preselect altitude is not raised at least 45 seconds before reaching the altitude constraint waypoint, CHECK PRESELECTOR shows. If raised before reaching, VNAV sequences to VFLC and resumes climb after crossing the waypoint.

When the aircraft is within capture distance of the constraint altitude, the VNAV mode automatically sequences to VALTS or VALTV, and remains in VALTS, VALTV, or VALT until a climb is resumed. The PFD shows an altitude capture after the mode switch. If the capture altitude is not the same as the preselect altitude, an aural alert is issued when the aircraft is within 1000 ft of the capture.

Overspeed (OSPD) Mode is automatically activated when the aircraft Mach number is more than Mmo + 0.01, or the airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt. In OSPD Mode, the system generates pitch commands to reduce airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. The speed reference is Mmo - 0.02 or Vmo - 10 kt. The SPEED Knob is inhibited, and other vertical modes are inhibited unless in ALTS, ALT, TO, or GA Mode. AT is armed in OSPD Mode, and the system returns to FLC Mode when airspeed is below the limit.

Underspeed (USPD) Mode is automatically activated when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01, unless ALTS mode is captured or ALT mode is active. An amber USPD symbol is displayed on the FMA, and an aural alert "underspeed" is given. Underspeed Protection Mode is inhibited if Radio Altitude is below 1000 ft or after GS mode is captured.

incompatible Modes will be automatically deselected
In the PTCH Mode, the FG generates commands to hold the actual aircraft pitch angle at Mode selection.

The ALTS Mode is always armed, except when ALT, GS, or GA Mode is active. When the vertical Mode is GA, ALTS is armed if the preselected altitude is greater than the current altitude by 75 ft. Rotating the ALT knob on the FCP inhibits ALTS Mode to prevent altitude capture during preselected altitude changes. ALTS Mode is activated during altitude capture when a new altitude is selected or the current altitude is maintained. When ALTS Mode is activated, the ROLL Mode remains unchanged. The ALTS Mode is activated when the preselected altitude changes during ALTS Mode capture.
The Altitude Hold Mode (ALT) is activated to maintain a selected barometric pressure altitude.
The Vertical Speed (VS) Mode holds a preselected vertical speed.

The FLC Mode controls pitch to maintain the commanded Indicated Airspeed (IAS) or Mach speed. It generates commands to hold the selected airspeed/Mach or the minimum vertical speed, to achieve preselected target altitude. When holding the airspeed/Mach reference or the minimum vertical speed, the FG generates a greater closure rate to reach the target altitude.
FMS select the Mode of ALTS, ALT, VS, FLC, Path or Glidepath automatically.
The GS Mode generates commands to capture or track the selected glideslope.
The TO Mode can be deselected in any of the following ways: – Changing the FG coupled side. – Manually selecting other vertical modes.

The Go-around (GA) Mode can be selected by pressing the TOGA Pushbutton when the aircraft is in flight. It can be deselected by changing the FG coupled side or manually selecting other lateral or vertical modes. While GA mode is active, pitch angle is commanded according to the go-around target speed, with an initial lower limit of 8° that reduces to 4°. The FD pitch command upper limit expands to 30°, but the AP pitch control upper limit remains at 20°. The go-around target speed is the greater of VAPP and current speed, ranging from VREF + 5 kt to VREF + 20 kt during two-engine operation, and VREF + 5 kt to VREF + 15 kt during single-engine operation.
In the OSPD Mode, the system generates pitch commands as required to reduce the airspeed below Vmo/Mmo.

The Underspeed (USPD) Mode automatically activates when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01. It provides pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman to prevent stall. The mode exits automatically when airspeed/Mach is greater than Vman/Mman, switching the vertical mode to FLC. USPD is inhibited below 1000 ft after takeoff, after GS capture during ILS approach, and in ALT or ALTS Mode during cruise.

The Windshear Escape Mode (WS) automatically switches the lateral mode to GA and the vertical mode to WS when TAWS triggers a windshear warning. It generates optimal escape maneuver commands integrating airspeed, radio altitude, and AOA data until windshear warnings cease, and AT is set to TOGA thrust.

If the preselect altitude is not raised to the flight plan target altitude or above, it will be captured, causing the mode to sequence to VALTS. When the aircraft is within capture distance of a constraint altitude, VNAV mode automatically sequences to altitude hold modes (VALTS or VALTV during climb, or altitude hold during descent) and remains in that mode until a climb or descent is resumed. If the capture altitude differs from the preselect altitude, an aural alert sounds when the aircraft is within 1000 ft of the capture altitude. In altitude hold mode, pitch is controlled to maintain the commanded altitude.

When overspeed occurs, the OSPD Mode is automatically activated unless ALTS Mode or ALT Mode are activated or GS Mode is captured. The overspeed condition means that the aircraft Mach number is more than Mmo + 0.01, or the airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt. In the OSPD Mode, the system generates pitch commands as required to reduce the airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. The speed reference is Mmo - 0.02 or Vmo - 10 kt. When OSPD mode is active, the SPEED Knob will be inhibited. When underspeed occurs, the USPD Mode is automatically activated unless ALTS mode is captured or ALT mode is active. The underspeed condition is defined when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01.
When the airspeed is more than Vman - 5 kt or Mman - 0.01 M, selecting other vertical mode cancels USPD mode. Or If the airspeed increases to Vman/Mman, the USPD Mode exits automatically.

- Pitch (PTCH) Mode: Hold preselected pitch angle.

- Takeoff (TO) Mode: Vertical Guidance based on takeoff target speed.
- Go-around (GA) Mode: Vertical Guidance based on go-around target speed.
- Overspeed (OSPD) Mode: Hold fixed indicated airspeed or Mach number.
- Underspeed (USPD) Mode: Hold fixed indicated airspeed or Mach number.

Responses: The Autoflight System automatically manages and controls the lateral and vertical flight path of the aircraft using information from the FMS, radio navigation aids, or pilot input. It consists of two Flight Generators (FGs), two Flight Directors (FDs), one Autopilot (AP), one Autothrottle (AT), three Yaw Dampers (YDs), and one Mach Trim system. The AP controls pitch and roll, the AT controls engine thrust, and the YDs provide damping and turning coordination. The Mach Trim system generates horizontal stabilizer trim commands based on Mach changes. The system's software is hosted in the Integrated Processing System, and control is managed through the Flight Control Panel (FCP), control wheels, and thrust levers. The OSPD Mode is designed to generate pitch commands as required to reduce the airspeed below Vmo/Mmo.

The USPD Mode is automatically activated when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01, unless ALTS mode is captured or ALT mode is active. It generates pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman. The mode deactivates automatically when the current airspeed/Mach is greater than Vman/Mman, with the airspeed reference then set to Vman + 5 kt/Mman + 0.01. During USPD Mode, the SPEED Knob is inhibited, and other vertical modes are inhibited unless in ALTS, ALT, TO, or GA Mode. The AP reverts to armed, and AT is armed. USPD Mode is inhibited below 1000 ft after takeoff and after GS capture during an ILS approach, and will not activate in ALT or ALTS Mode during cruise.

The Autobest System provides windshear recovery guidance by sending calculated pitch and roll maneuver commands. After the TAWS sends a windshear warning, the Flight Director will first send a nose-up command of 15° or below the Alpha Margin Indicator (AMI), whichever is lower. As the acceleration rate increases, the command bar is relatively far from AMI (pitch attitude not bigger than 2°) to achieve a greater climb rate. After the windshear condition disappears, the command bar is 15° or slightly below AMI pitch attitude, whichever is lower. The system generates optimal escape maneuver commands integrating airspeed, radio altitude, and AOA data.

The FG generates commands to hold the bank angle or the heading according to the bank angle value when the Mode is activated. When the current bank angle of the aircraft is greater than 5°, the aircraft maintains the current bank angle. When the current bank angle is smaller than or equal to 5°, the aircraft maintains the existing heading in the ROLL Mode.
The vertical Mode, lateral Mode and AT Mode show on the FMA at the top of the PFD.
cognize and understand the active and armed Modes of the Autoflight System
The vertical modes are engaged and disengaged through the related pushbuttons on the Flight Control Panel (FCP).
When a vertical Mode is selected, incompatible Modes will be automatically deselected.
The PTCH Mode commands the Flight Director (FG) to hold the actual aircraft pitch angle at the time of Mode selection.

The ALTS Mode is always armed, except when ALT, GS, or GA Mode is active. When GA Mode is active, ALTS is armed if the preselected altitude is 75 ft greater than the current altitude. Rotating the ALT knob on the FCP inhibits ALTS to prevent altitude capture during preselected altitude changes. In ALTS Mode, the FG commands capture or follow of the preselected barometric altitude. If VNAV is not engaged, the FCP's preselected altitude is used. If VNAV is engaged, the FMS target altitude can also be used, with the FG selecting the closest altitude. If the FCP preselected altitude matches the FMS target, the FCP altitude is used. If the FMS target is captured as reference, green "ALTV" is displayed. ALTS responds to barometric reference setting changes. Changing the preselected altitude during ALT capture or while ALTS is engaged activates ALT Mode, with the new altitude becoming the reference. AT controls airspeed in ALTS Mode. ALTS deselects if ALT, GS, or GA Mode is activated.
The Altitude Hold Mode (ALT) is activated to acquire and maintain the current pressure altitude.

The Vertical Speed (VS) Mode is selected by pressing the VS Button on the Flight Control Panel (FCP). In the VS Mode, the Autoflight System generates commands to maintain the VS reference. The PITCH/VS Wheel is used to change the VS reference. The vertical speed reference is limited to ± 8000 ft/min.

The FLC Mode controls pitch to maintain the commanded Indicated Airspeed (IAS) or Mach speed. It also generates commands to hold the selected airspeed/Mach or the minimum vertical speed, to achieve preselected target altitude.

Once VNAV is active, FMS can automatically select the vertical Mode as required. It will automatically select ALTS, ALT, VS or FLC based on the vertical constraints of the flight plan. In VNAV Mode, Path and Glidepath Modes may also be selected by the FMS.
The GS Mode generates commands to capture or track the selected glideslope.
The TO Mode is activated. AP is engaged, and TO Mode is cancelled.

The Go-around (GA) Mode can be selected by pressing the TOGA Pushbutton when the aircraft is in flight. It can be deselected by changing the FG coupled side, manually selecting other lateral or vertical modes, or by pressing the SYNC Pushbutton. When active in the roll axis, it commands the aircraft to hold the heading reference with a bank angle limited to ± 5°. In the vertical axis, it commands pitch angle in accordance with the go-around target speed, with a pitch command upper limit of 30° for the FD and 20° for the AP. The FMA displays "GA" in green for this mode. The Automatic Takeoff Thrust Control System (ATTCS) is automatically engaged during the Go-Around Phase.

The OSPD Mode automatically activates when the aircraft's Mach number exceeds Mmo + 0.01 or airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt. It generates pitch commands to reduce airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. The speed reference in OSPD Mode is Mmo - 0.02 or Vmo - 10 kt. When the airspeed is below this limit, the system returns to FLC Mode.

When underspeed occurs (airspeed less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach less than Mman - 0.01), the USPD Mode is automatically activated unless ALTS mode is captured or ALT mode is active. An amber USPD symbol is displayed, and an "underspeed" aural alert sounds. The AP and AT provide commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman. USPD mode deactivates when airspeed exceeds Vman + 5 kt or Mman + 0.01, switching to FLC Mode with the altitude reference unchanged. The SPEED Knob is inhibited in USPD Mode, and other vertical modes are also inhibited unless in ALTS, ALT, TO, or GA Mode. AT is armed when USPD is active. USPD can be deselected manually by selecting another vertical mode when airspeed is above Vman - 5 kt or Mman - 0.01, or automatically when airspeed increases to Vman or Mman. Underspeed Protection is inhibited below 1000 ft after takeoff and after GS capture during an ILS approach.

The Windshear Escape Mode (WS) is automatically entered when the TAWS detects a windshear warning. It provides optimal escape maneuver commands by integrating airspeed, radio altitude, and AOA data until the windshear warnings cease. The Flight Director (FD) provides guidance commands from one active flight director (FG). Autothrust (AT) is set to TOGA thrust. The autopilot disengages automatically after 2 seconds. To manually exit WS mode, another vertical mode must be selected.

- EXT PWR: Amber for load value if status is displayed in green or load is not less than 100%.

- TRU: Amber if the corresponding TRU fails. Amber for load value if status is displayed in amber or load is more than 100%.
- MAIN BATT and APU BATT: Amber if MAIN (APU) BATT DISCHARGE or MAIN (APU) BATT FAULT or MAIN (APU) BATT TEMP SENS FAULT message is displayed on EICAS. - CHK FUEL AT ALTN (amber): It indicates that the computed fuel for the active flight plan alternate airport is less than the specified reserve fuel.
- CHK FUEL AT DEST (amber): It indicates that the computed fuel for the active flight plan destination airport is less than the specified reserve fuel.
- CHK POS (amber): Shows when the FMS position estimate does not meet the accuracy required for the current phase of flight.
- FMS NAV INVALID (amber): Shows when the aircraft is airborne and the FMS does not have a valid airspeed or heading.
- FMS DR (amber): Shows when the FMS is in DR mode and the aircraft has been airborne for longer than 2 min.

- LOI TERM (amber): Shows when the GNSS has a LOI within the terminal area.
- LOI (amber): Shows when the GNSS has a Loss Of Integrity.
- MSG (amber): Shows when there is an amber message on the CDU MESSAGES page.
- NO APPR (amber): Shows during final approach when the required navigation sensor or the required navigation accuracy to complete the approach is lost.
- SPD (amber): Shows when the current aircraft speed is 20 kt or more than the target speed and VNAV is selected. Overspeed (OSPD) Mode: Automatically activated when aircraft Mach number is more than Mmo + 0.01 or airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt. Generates pitch commands to reduce airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. Speed reference becomes Mmo - 0.02 or Vmo - 10 kt. The SPEED Knob is inhibited. AP reverts to arm (white ARM on FMA). Exiting OSPD Mode engages FLC Mode automatically, and AT enters CLB or IDLE Thrust Mode.

Underspeed (USPD) Mode: Automatically activated when airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01. Displays an amber USPD symbol and sounds an "underspeed" alert. Generates pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman. Speed reference becomes Vman + 5 kt or Mman + 0.01 upon exiting USPD. The FG vertical mode switches to FLC Mode. The SPEED Knob is inhibited. AP reverts to arm (white ARM on FMA). Exiting USPD Mode engages FLC Mode automatically, and AT enters CLB or IDLE Thrust Mode. Underspeed Protection Mode is inhibited below 1000 ft after takeoff, after GS capture during ILS approach, and in ALT or ALTS Mode during cruise.

The vertical modes are engaged and disengaged through the related pushbuttons on the Flight Control Panel (FCP). When a vertical Mode is selected, the incompatible Modes will be automatically deselected.
Incompatible Modes will be automatically deselected.

**Vertical Modes:**
*   **Pitch (PTCH) Mode:** Hold preselected pitch angle.
*   **Altitude Select (ALTS) Mode:** Capture preselected barometric altitude.
*   **Altitude Hold Mode (ALT):** Hold current barometric altitude.
*   **Vertical Speed Mode (VS):** Hold preselected vertical speed.
*   **Flight Level Change (FLC) Mode:** Hold airspeed or Mach number during climb or descent.
*   **Vertical Navigation (VNAV) Mode:** FMS selects ALTS, ALT, VS, FLC, Path or Glidepath automatically.
*   **Approach (APPR) Mode - Glideslope (GS) Mode:** Descend in accordance with the glideslope signal or the FMS command.
*   **Takeoff (TO) Mode:** Vertical guidance based on takeoff target speed.
*   **Go-around (GA) Mode:** Vertical guidance based on go-around target speed.
*   **Overspeed (OSPD) Mode:** Hold fixed indicated airspeed or Mach number.
*   **Underspeed (USPD) Mode:** Hold fixed indicated airspeed or Mach number.
*   **Windshear Escape Mode (WS):** Hold specified pitch angle and airspeed.

**Lateral Modes:**
*   **Roll (ROLL) Mode:** Hold the aircraft heading or the bank angle.
*   **1/2 Bank (1/2 BANK) Mode:** Reduce the bank angle limit to ± 12.5°.
*   **Heading Select (HDG) Mode:** Hold preselected heading.
*   **Lateral Navigation Mode (LNAV):** Fly in accordance with navigation sources (FMS, LOC, VOR) during en route flight.
*   **APPR Mode - Lateral:** Fly in accordance with navigation sources (FMS, LOC, VOR) during approach.
*   **Takeoff (TO) Mode - Lateral:** Hold the aircraft's heading reference.
*   **Go-around (GA) Mode - Lateral:** Hold the aircraft's current heading.

The FLC Mode controls pitch to maintain the commanded Indicated Airspeed (IAS) or Mach speed. It generates commands to hold the selected airspeed/Mach or the minimum vertical speed, to achieve preselected target altitude.

The VNAV Mode allows the Autoflight System to follow FMS vertical profile constraints and provides references for vertical navigation. It is activated when enabled and valid, which occurs when the navigation source is FMS with an active flight plan and a TO waypoint, or when the navigation source is LOC following a NAV-to-NAV capture, or when the navigation source is FMS and the active lateral Mode is LNAV or HDG with the aircraft within a predetermined deviation from the FMS flight plan. VNAV is armed by pressing the VNAV Button on the Flight Control Panel (FCP). Once active, the FMS can automatically select vertical Modes such as ALTS, ALT, VS, or FLC based on the flight plan's vertical constraints, providing corresponding altitude and speed references. Pilots can manually override these selections and reference values. In VNAV Mode, the FMS can also select Path Mode to track the FMS vertical path or Glidepath Mode to track the FMS vertical glidepath. The Autothrottle (AT) controls airspeed or thrust depending on the active vertical Mode. VNAV is inhibited if APPR Mode is in vertical approach capture or track state, or if the aircraft is in OSPD Mode. The TOGA Pushbutton deselects VNAV Mode.

The ALTS Mode is always armed except when ALT Mode, GS Mode or GA Mode is active. When GA Mode is active, ALTS Mode is armed if the preselected altitude is 75 ft greater than the current altitude. Rotating the ALT knob on the FCP inhibits ALTS Mode to prevent altitude capture during preselected altitude changes. ALTS Mode is activated during altitude capture or when maintaining the current altitude. ALTS Mode deselects if ALT Mode, GS Mode or GA Mode is activated. The FG generates commands to capture or follow the preselected barometric altitude. The FG uses the barometric altitude preselected by rotating the ALT knob as the reference if VNAV is not engaged. If VNAV is activated, the FMS target altitude can also be used as a reference, and the FG compares both and uses the closest altitude. When the preselected altitude on the FCP matches the FMS target altitude, the FCP preselected altitude is used. If the FMS target altitude is captured as the reference, "ALTV" is displayed. ALTS Mode responds to changes in barometric reference settings. If the preselected altitude changes during ALT capture or when ALTS Mode is engaged, ALT Mode will become active, and the new preselected altitude will be the reference. In ALTS Mode, the AT controls airspeed.
In the ALT Mode, the Autoflight System generates commands to acquire and maintain the current pressure altitude when the Mode is selected.
Hold preselected vertical speed.

The FLC Mode controls pitch to maintain a commanded Indicated Airspeed (IAS) or Mach speed during climb or descent, generating commands to achieve a preselected target altitude with a greater closure rate. It can be selected by pressing the FLC Button on the Flight Control Panel (FCP). If the current vertical Mode is OSPD, the FG commands a reversion to FLC Mode when the overspeed condition ceases. When an altitude constraint or preselect altitude is encountered during a climb, the FLC mode is used in conjunction with an altitude hold mode. The FLC Mode also shows as VFLC on the PFD during a VNAV climb. If the preselected altitude changes while in FLC Mode, the mode will adjust to climb or descend towards the new altitude. Once the target altitude is reached, the FG automatically changes to Altitude Select (ALTS) Mode.
VNAV Mode automatically selects ALTS, ALT, VS, FLC, Path, or Glidepath based on the vertical constraints of the flight plan.

The APPR Mode generates commands in the lateral axis to track and capture the selected navigation source (FMS/LOC/VOR). For precision approaches, when the APPR Mode is armed, the related vertical Mode is activated. In the APPR Mode, the AT controls airspeed.

The Overspeed (OSPD) Mode automatically activates when the aircraft Mach number is more than Mmo + 0.01, or the airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt. The system generates pitch commands to reduce the airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. The Underspeed (USPD) Mode automatically activates when the aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01. The system generates pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman.

The Windshear Escape Mode (WS) is automatically entered when the TAWS detects a windshear warning. It provides optimal escape maneuver commands by integrating airspeed, radio altitude, and AOA data until the windshear warnings cease. The Autopilot disengages automatically after 2 seconds, and AT is set to TOGA thrust.
The ALT Mode can be activated manually or automatically. It can be deselected by pressing the ALT Button on the Flight Control Panel (FCP) or by activating other vertical modes.

During all flight operations, it is critical for the pilot to recognize and understand the active and armed Modes of the Autoflight System.

The vertical modes are engaged and disengaged through the related pushbuttons on the Flight Control Panel (FCP). When a vertical Mode is selected, the incompatible Modes will be automatically deselected.
incompatible Modes will be automatically deselected.
In the PTCH Mode, the FG generates commands to hold the actual aircraft pitch angle at Mode selection.

The ALTS Mode is always armed, except when the ALT, GS, or GA Mode is active. When the vertical Mode is GA, the ALTS Mode is armed if the preselected altitude is greater than the current altitude by 75 ft. Rotating the ALT knob on the Flight Control Panel (FCP) will inhibit the ALTS Mode to prevent altitude capture during preselected altitude change. The ALTS Mode deselects if ALT Mode, GS Mode, or GA Mode is activated. When the aircraft is in the ALTS Mode, the FG generates commands to capture or follow the preselected barometric altitude reference. If VNAV is not engaged, the FG uses the barometric altitude preselected by rotating the ALT knob on the FCP. If VNAV is activated, the FMS target altitude can also be used as a valid reference, and the FG compares it with the FCP preselected altitude, using the closer one. The AT controls airspeed in ALTS Mode. The Autoflight System responds to changes in barometric reference setting in ALTS Mode. If the preselected altitude changes during ALT capture or when ALTS mode is engaged, ALT mode will be active and the new preselected altitude becomes the reference.

The FLC Mode controls pitch to maintain the commanded Indicated Airspeed (IAS) or Mach speed. It generates commands to hold the selected airspeed/Mach or the minimum vertical speed to achieve a preselected target altitude, generating a greater closure rate to reach the target.

Once VNAV is active, FMS can automatically select the vertical Mode as required. It will automatically select ALTS, ALT, VS or FLC based on the vertical constraints of the flight plan, and provide the altitude and speed references in these Modes.
Go-around (GA) Mode is activated when the aircraft needs to abort a landing or go around for another approach.

Both Overspeed (OSPD) and Underspeed (USPD) Modes activate automatically when a respective overspeed or underspeed condition occurs, and in both modes, the AP does not disengage but reverts to an armed state.
The Windshear Escape Mode (WS) is designed to provide escape maneuver commands integrating airspeed, radio altitude, and AOA data until windshear warnings cease.

The Refuel Shutoff Valve is manually selected open to start refueling. The Fuel Quantity Computer (FQC) monitors the refueling process and automatically controls the Refuel Shutoff Valve to close when fuel in the tank reaches the preselected quantity. This mode ensures fuel quantities between left and right tanks are balanced. If an imbalance of more than 400 kg (882 lb) occurs, the tank with the higher quantity is shutoff. Once balanced, both tanks are refueled. In Automatic Refueling Mode, the REFUEL SELECTION Switch is set to AUTO. The INCR/DECRT Switch is used to set the required refuel quantity. The Refuel Shutoff Valve is manually selected open to start refueling. The Fuel Quantity Computer (FQC) monitors the refueling process and automatically controls the Refuel Shutoff Valve to close when fuel in the tank reaches the preselected quantity. The FQC automatically records the last preselected refuel quantity and displays it on the refuel/defuel indicator. Automatic Refueling Mode ensures that fuel quantities between the left and right fuel tanks are balanced upon completion of refueling.

- White: The corresponding generator is inoperative.
- Green: The corresponding generator operates normally.
- Amber: TRU fails.
- Magenta: Data invalid.

For L/R Generator: White: The status of the corresponding generator is displayed in white. Green: The status of the corresponding generator is displayed in green and the load of the corresponding generator is not more than 100 %. For APU Generator: White: The status of the APU GEN is displayed in white. Green: The status of the APU GEN is displayed in green and the load of the APU GEN is not more than 100 %. Operating Modes, Principle of Primary Flight Control System

The Flap/Slat Control System controls three leading-edge slats and two trailing-edge flaps for each wing. These are electrically controlled and actuated. The system protects against skew and asymmetry by stopping Power Drive Units (PDUs) and cutting out the system if detected. The pilot uses the FLP/SLT Handle or FLP/SLT OVRD Switch to command the Flap/Slat Electronic Control Unit (FSECU), which then signals the PDUs to extend or retract flaps and slats. The FSECU has independent flap and slat channels, and the PDUs have two DC motors. Failure of one FSECU channel, one PDU motor, or one flap/slat channel causes operation at half speed. Slats extend before flaps during extension, and flaps retract before slats during retraction. The FLP/SLT OVRD Switch can override the FLP/SLT Handle. Flap and slat positions are displayed on the EICAS with a pointer, which disappears if data is invalid. The pointer color indicates operational status: Green for normal, Cyan for half speed, and Amber for failed. The flap/slat operating status indication is hidden when flaps/slats are retracted, landing gear is retracted and locked, and brake temperature is normal for over 30 seconds.

Mach trim function enhances the aircraft stability for manual flight at high Mach numbers. Controls and Indications, Operating Modes, Principle of Primary Flight Control System

The Flap/Slat Control System controls three leading-edge slats and two trailing-edge flaps for each wing. These devices are electrically controlled and actuated to increase wing lift and decrease stall speed. The system includes Flap/Slat Electronic Control Units (FSECUs) and Power Drive Units (PDUs). The FSECU receives commands from the FLP/SLT Handle or FLP/SLT OVRD Switch and sends signals to the PDUs to drive the flap and slat actuators. The FSECUs have independent flap and slat channels. Flap/slat skew and asymmetry are detected by sensors and monitored by the FSECU, which will stop operation and lock the system if detected. The flaps/slats are displayed on the EICAS with a pointer indicating their position and color-coded status (green for normal, cyan for half speed, amber for failed). The operating status can be hidden under specific conditions. The system also has an interlock function that restricts movement based on airspeed and aircraft state (ground/air), and limits extension to FLAP 3 when the RAT is extended.

Each control column has one stick shaker, and each Stall Protection Computer (SPC) can drive both stick shakers simultaneously.
The Stall Protection Computer (SPC) commands the AP pitch servo motor to activate the stick pusher. Only when both SPCs generate stall pusher commands simultaneously, will the stick pusher activate.

It adjusts bleed air via the PACKs, delivering conditioned air to the cabin, cockpit, avionics compartment, and cargo compartment, with exhaust air discharged via the outflow valve. When the aircraft is on the ground, an external ground air conditioning unit can supply conditioned air to the mixing manifold for cabin ventilation.
The bleed air from the pneumatic system is adjusted through the two flow control valves, temperature and pressure are adjusted through two PACKs.

xhaust air is discharged via the outflow valve.

The TOD location shows on both the PPOS and PLAN maps. TOD also shows on the MFD ACT FPLN PROGRESS text page to show the relationship of the TOD location relative to other flight plan waypoints. The FMS continuously calculates the TOD location. If there is an altitude hold segment that follows an altitude constraint waypoint, TOD also shows at the top of the second descent segment. If the aircraft is close to the descent path, and is not at a planned altitude that intercepts the path, the FMS recalculates the TOD location based on the intersection of the current altitude and the descent path. The aircraft is considered to be close to the descent path when it is 50 NM or 20 % of the distance from origin to the destination, whichever is smaller (but not less than 6 NM). 1 min before the aircraft intercepts the planned descent path, TOD shows on the PFD message line. If the flight plan target altitude is different from the current preselect altitude, the new target altitude shows on the PFD. The new flight plan target altitude is the next altitude constraint. 45 s before the aircraft reaches the TOD, if the preselect altitude has not been lowered, the message CHECK PRESELECTOR shows on the CDU, and MSG shows on the PFD. 5 s before the aircraft reaches the TOD, the annunciation TOD flashes on the PFD and an aural alert is sounded. If the preselector altitude is set lower than the current altitude of the aircraft before the aircraft reaches the TOD, the VNAV automatically preset VPATH mode, and the descent starts when the aircraft reaches the TOD. If the preselector altitude is not set lower than the current altitude of the aircraft before the aircraft reaches the TOD, VNAV holds the VALT mode. If the aircraft is about to intersect the planned descent path, VNAV captures the path, even if the altitude at the capture point is not a flight planned target altitude and not a planned TOD. The VNAV mode automatically select VPATH mode descent if the preselect altitude is lowered before the aircraft reaches the descent path intersection.

Refueling can be performed by pressure or gravity. Pressure refueling uses AC or DC power. Gravity refueling is done through two receptacles on the wings. Refueling pressure should not exceed 55 psi. There are two modes of pressure refueling: automatic and manual. Automatic refueling balances fuel quantities between tanks. Refueling is controlled via the Refuel/Defuel Control Panel. The HF communication system should not be used during refueling.

The potable water system stores water in an 83 L tank in the forward cargo compartment and distributes it to galleys and lavatories. The system can be pressurized by air compressors (in-flight or on the ground) or a ground air source. Manual shut-off valves are located in galleys and lavatories. Water quantity is displayed on the forward attendant panel and the water system interface panel. The waste water system has a 68 L tank, serviced via the waste service panel on the aft fuselage. Toilet flushing uses differential pressure, either from cabin/tank pressure difference at altitude or a vacuum generator at lower altitudes. System status is shown on the water/waste status panel on the forward attendant panel.
